claims.claimed_en: systemin
claims.evidence_en: The preferred transgenic (genetically modified) plants or plant cultivars to be treated according to the invention include all plants which, through the genetic modification, received genetic material that confers particularly advantageous, useful properties ("traits") on these plants. Examples of such properties are better plant growth, increased tolerance to high or low temperatures, increased tolerance to drought or to water or soil salt content, increased flowering performance, easier harvesting, acceleration of ripening, higher crop yields, higher quality and/or higher nutritional value of the harvested products, better storability and/or processability of the harvested products. Further and particularly emphasised examples of such properties are an increased defence of the plants against animal and microbial pests, such as against insects, mites, phytopathogenic fungi, bacteria and/or viruses, and also an increased tolerance of the plants to certain herbicidal active ingredients. Examples of transgenic plants mentioned are the important crop plants, such as cereals (wheat, rice), soya, potato, cotton, oilseed rape and in particular maize, and also fruit plants (with the fruits apples, pears, citrus fruits and grapes), maize in particular, but also soya, potato, cotton and oilseed rape, being especially emphasised. Properties ("traits") especially emphasised are the increased defence of the plants against insects by toxins formed in the plants, in particular those which are produced in the plants by the genetic material from Bacillus thuringiensis (for example by the genes CrylA(a), CrylA(b), CrylA(c), CryIIA, CrylIIIA, CrylIIIB2, Cry9c, Cry2Ab, Cry3Bb and CrylF, and combinations thereof) (hereinafter "Bt plants"). Properties ("traits") also especially emphasised are the increased defence of plants against fungi, bacteria and viruses by systemic acquired resistance (SAR), systemin, phytoalexins, elicitors, and also resistance genes and correspondingly expressed proteins and toxins. Properties ("traits") furthermore especially emphasised are the increased tolerance of the plants to certain herbicidal active ingredients, for example imidazolinones, sulfonylureas, glyphosate or phosphinothricin (for example the "PAT" gene). The genes conferring the respective desired properties ("traits") may also occur in combination with one another in the transgenic plants. Examples of "Bt plants" which may be mentioned are above all maize varieties, but likewise cotton varieties, soya varieties and potato varieties, sold under the trade names YIELD GARD(R) (for example maize, cotton, soya), KnockOut(R) (for example maize), StarLink(R) (for example maize), Bollgard(R) (cotton), Nucotn(R) (cotton) and NewLeaf(R) (potato). Examples of herbicide-tolerant plants which may be mentioned are above all maize varieties, but likewise cotton varieties and soya varieties, sold under the trade names Roundup Ready(R) (tolerance to glyphosate, for example maize, cotton, soya), Liberty Link(R) (tolerance to phosphinothricin, for example oilseed rape), IMI(R) (tolerance to imidazolinones) and STS(R) (tolerance to sulfonylureas, for example maize). Herbicide-resistant plants (bred conventionally for herbicide tolerance) which may be mentioned also include the varieties sold under the name Clearfield(R) (for example maize). It goes without saying that these statements also apply to plant cultivars developed in the future, or coming onto the market in the future, having these or genetic properties developed in the future ("traits").

claims.evidence_en: Because of its stability, crystal modification I is outstandingly suitable for the preparation of formulations, in particular suspension formulations of crop protection agents. The invention therefore also provides crop protection agents which contain crystal modification I of tembotrione alone or in a mixture with auxiliaries and carriers, and also in a mixture with other active ingredients. The invention also includes mixtures of crystal modification I of tembotrione with crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione, for example those which occur at any point of the conversion process according to the invention of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, into crystal modification I. An active ingredient quality with more than 20 wt.-% of crystal modification I of tembotrione is preferred, particularly preferably with more than 90 wt.-%, very particularly preferably with more than 95 wt.-% and most preferably with more than 98 wt.-%. If appropriate, tembotrione in crystal modification I is mixed with one or more other herbicides. Such mixtures too benefit from the advantageous properties of the crystal modification I according to the invention. Because of its stability, crystal modification I of tembotrione is quite generally suitable as starting material for the preparation of any crop protection formulations containing tembotrione, even if after formulation the tembotrione is no longer present in this form but for instance in dissolved form. The invention therefore also provides processes for the preparation of crop protection formulations containing tembotrione which use crystal modification I of tembotrione, and also crop protection formulations containing tembotrione which have been obtained from crystal modification I of tembotrione. The use of crystal modification I increases the safety of preparations of tembotrione and thus reduces the risk of incorrect dosing. Crystal modification I of tembotrione can be converted in a known manner into the customary formulations, such as suspension concentrates, colloidal concentrates, dispersible concentrates, emulsifiable concentrates (emulsion concentrates), emulsion seed dressings, suspension seed dressings, granules, microgranules, suspoemulsions, oil dispersions, water-soluble granules, water-soluble concentrates and water-dispersible granules, using suitable auxiliaries and carriers or solvents. The active compound should here be present in a concentration of about 0.5 to 90 wt.-% of the total mixture, that is to say in amounts which are sufficient to reach the necessary dosage level. The formulations are prepared, for example, by extending crystal modification I of tembotrione with solvents and/or carriers, if appropriate using emulsifiers and/or dispersants, and/or other auxiliaries such as, for example, penetration aids.

claims.evidence_en: Tembotrione in crystal modification I exhibits an outstanding herbicidal action against representatives of the group of both monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous plants. The invention therefore also provides the use of crystal modification I of tembotrione for the preparation of a crop protection agent for the treatment of weed infestation. By virtue of its high tolerance by crop plants, the crystal modification I of tembotrione according to the invention is suitable for controlling unwanted plants in crops of, for example, wheat, barley, oats, rye, rice, maize, sugar beet, sugar cane, cotton and soya, in particular in rice, maize and sugar cane. According to the invention, all plants and plant parts can be treated. Plants are here understood to mean all plants and plant populations, such as desired and undesired wild plants or crop plants (including naturally occurring crop plants). Crop plants can be plants which can be obtained by conventional breeding and optimization methods or by biotechnological and genetic engineering methods or by combinations of these methods, including the transgenic plants and including the plant varieties protectable or not protectable by plant variety rights. Plant parts are to be understood as meaning all above-ground and below-ground parts and organs of the plants, such as shoot, leaf, flower and root, the examples given being leaves, needles, stalks, stems, flowers, fruiting bodies, fruits and seeds, and also roots, tubers and rhizomes. Plant parts also include harvested material and vegetative and generative propagation material, for example cuttings, tubers, rhizomes, offshoots and seeds. The treatment according to the invention of the plants and plant parts with the crystal modification I of tembotrione according to the invention is effected directly or by action on their surroundings, habitat or storage space, by the customary treatment methods, e.g. by dipping, spraying, evaporating, fogging, scattering or brushing on.

evidence_lines.text_en: Thermodynamically stable crystal modification of 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione

A thermodynamically stable crystal modification of the herbicidal active ingredient 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl) cyclohexane-1,3-dione (tembotrione) is described. This thermodynamically stable crystal modification shows particular advantages in the stability of suspension formulations.

More particularly it relates to a thermodynamically stable crystal modification of 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione of the formula [STRUCTURAL FORMULA: see drawings[0]], (hereinafter referred to as tembotrione), processes for its preparation and its use as a herbicide.

A thermodynamically stable modification of tembotrione crystallising in an orthorhombic system has been found which does not have the disadvantages mentioned above and is therefore particularly suitable for the preparation of suspension formulations such as suspension concentrates, suspoemulsions and oil dispersions.

In what follows, the terms "stable modification I", "stable crystal modification I", "thermodynamically stable modification I" and "thermodynamically stable crystal modification I" are understood as synonymous.

The stable modification has a melting point of 124.0 degrees C, a characteristic Raman spectrum (Fig. 1) and a characteristic infrared spectrum (Fig. 1a). It is referred to hereinafter as crystal modification I.
The single-crystal structure analysis of crystal modification I of tembotrione shows bond angles and bond lengths characteristic of this crystal modification, which are given in Table 3.
X-ray powder diffractometry of crystal modification I of tembotrione shows peaks characteristic of this crystal modification, which are given in Table 5.
Further crystallographic data of crystal modifications I and II of tembotrione are given in Table 7.

Description of the figures. Figure 1 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification I of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 1a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification I of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2. Figure 2 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification II of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 2a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification II of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2. Figure 3 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification III of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 3a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification III of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2.

The y axis carries no caption and no unit; labelled ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, printed with a decimal point and not a decimal comma. Zero is at the bottom and the bands point UPWARD; the top of the frame corresponds to about 0.94. The baseline sits close to zero. Roughly 80 to 100 distinguishable bands are visible: a cluster in the CH stretching region around 2900 to 3100, a largely empty stretch between about 2800 and 1700, and a densely populated fingerprint region below 1700. The most prominent bands are at approximately 2930 and 2970 (heights about 0.70 and 0.65), 2890 (about 0.44), 1670 (about 0.43), 1590 (about 0.42) and 1150 (about 0.46). At the extreme right hand edge, near about 100 cm-1, stands the tallest line on the sheet, reaching almost the top of the frame at about 0.93. Every one of these positions is read off the plot and is approximate only; the exact values are printed in Tabelle 1 and Tabelle 2 and must be taken from there. Full-page figure, set landscape (rotated 90 degrees) on the portrait sheet. Apart from the running header 'EP 2 045 236 A1' and the page number '18' the sheet carries no text; the only figure caption printed on the sheet reads, verbatim, 'Fig. 2a'. What is plotted is an infrared spectrum, a single continuous trace inside a rectangular frame. Shape of the trace: an almost flat baseline from about 4000 down to about 1750 cm-1, with only very weak features around 3000 to 2900 cm-1. Band structure begins abruptly at about 1700 cm-1. Between roughly 1700 and 600 cm-1 there is a densely populated fingerprint region with, very roughly, 35 to 45 distinguishable maxima. The strongest band is at approximately 1100 cm-1 (height about 0.47), with a nearly equal one immediately beside it at approximately 1140 cm-1; other prominent bands sit at approximately 1290 cm-1 (about 0.35), approximately 965 cm-1 (about 0.32) and approximately 650 cm-1 (about 0.29). Every one of these positions was read coarsely off the plot and is stated as an approximation only. The exact values are printed in the tables in the description and are not taken from this sheet.

evidence_lines.text_en: In the context of the present invention it was found that, besides the stable modification crystallising in an orthorhombic system, tembotrione also occurs in at least two metastable modifications.

The one metastable modification has a melting point of 123.9 degrees C, a characteristic Raman spectrum (Fig. 2) and a characteristic infrared spectrum (Fig. 2a). It is referred to hereinafter as crystal modification II.
The single-crystal structure analysis of crystal modification II of tembotrione shows bond angles and bond lengths characteristic of this crystal modification, which are given in Table 4.
X-ray powder diffractometry of crystal modification II of tembotrione shows peaks characteristic of this crystal modification, which are given in Table 6.
Further crystallographic data of crystal modifications I and II of tembotrione are given in Table 7.

Description of the figures. Figure 1 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification I of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 1a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification I of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2. Figure 2 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification II of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 2a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification II of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2. Figure 3 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification III of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 3a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification III of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2.

evidence_lines.text_en: Thermodynamically stable crystal modification of 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione

A thermodynamically stable crystal modification of the herbicidal active ingredient 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl) cyclohexane-1,3-dione (tembotrione) is described. This thermodynamically stable crystal modification shows particular advantages in the stability of suspension formulations.

More particularly it relates to a thermodynamically stable crystal modification of 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione of the formula [STRUCTURAL FORMULA: see drawings[0]], (hereinafter referred to as tembotrione), processes for its preparation and its use as a herbicide.

A thermodynamically stable modification of tembotrione crystallising in an orthorhombic system has been found which does not have the disadvantages mentioned above and is therefore particularly suitable for the preparation of suspension formulations such as suspension concentrates, suspoemulsions and oil dispersions.

In what follows, the terms "stable modification I", "stable crystal modification I", "thermodynamically stable modification I" and "thermodynamically stable crystal modification I" are understood as synonymous.

The stable modification has a melting point of 124.0 degrees C, a characteristic Raman spectrum (Fig. 1) and a characteristic infrared spectrum (Fig. 1a). It is referred to hereinafter as crystal modification I.
The single-crystal structure analysis of crystal modification I of tembotrione shows bond angles and bond lengths characteristic of this crystal modification, which are given in Table 3.
X-ray powder diffractometry of crystal modification I of tembotrione shows peaks characteristic of this crystal modification, which are given in Table 5.
Further crystallographic data of crystal modifications I and II of tembotrione are given in Table 7.

Description of the figures. Figure 1 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification I of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 1a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification I of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2. Figure 2 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification II of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 2a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification II of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2. Figure 3 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification III of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 3a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification III of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2.

claims.evidence_en: The conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I takes place at temperatures below 100°C, preferably at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C, particularly preferably at temperatures of 60°C to 80°C, very particularly preferably at temperatures of 50°C to 80°C. The duration of the conversion depends on the temperature and on the type of solvent. The duration of the conversion further depends on whether seed crystals of crystal modification I are used. In general, when the crystals of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, are completely dissolved at elevated temperature, the conversion into crystal modification I can be achieved directly by cooling crystallisation to room temperature without the use of seed crystals. Cooling to room temperature is preferably carried out at a cooling rate of less than 25°C, particularly preferably at a cooling rate of less than 20°C. The conversion of a suspension of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, can as a rule be brought about within a period of 14 days without the use of seed crystals. If seed crystals of crystal modification I are used in the conversion of a suspension, a treatment time of 24 to 48 hours is in general sufficient to achieve quantitative conversion of the crystals into crystal modification I. 2 g of tembotrione were dissolved completely in acetone at the boil (56 degrees C) and then cooled slowly, i.e. at a cooling rate of less than 20 degrees C/h, down to room temperature. The crystals are filtered off and dried at temperatures below 60 degrees C. 2 g of tembotrione were dissolved completely in ethanol at the boil (78°C). The clear solution was then cooled slowly, i.e. at a cooling rate of less than 20°C/h, down to 7°C. The crystallisate is filtered off and dried at temperatures < 60°C. 2 g of tembotrione were dissolved completely in toluene at the boil (111°C). The clear solution was then cooled slowly, i.e. at a cooling rate of less than 20°C/h, down to 7°C. The crystallisate is filtered off and dried at temperatures < 60°C.

claims.evidence_en: Thermodynamically stable crystal modification of 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione A thermodynamically stable crystal modification of the herbicidal active ingredient 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl) cyclohexane-1,3-dione (tembotrione) is described. This thermodynamically stable crystal modification shows particular advantages in the stability of suspension formulations. More particularly it relates to a thermodynamically stable crystal modification of 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione of the formula [STRUCTURAL FORMULA: see drawings[0]], (hereinafter referred to as tembotrione), processes for its preparation and its use as a herbicide. Drawn on the page: 1 structure. C17H16ClF3O6S (CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)C2C(=O)CCCC2=O)c(Cl)c1COCC(F)(F)F). The tembotrione known for example from WO 00/21924 (Example No. 3 in Table 1 there) has herbicidal properties and is suitable for the preparation of crop protection agents used for weed control. However, it has been found that the tembotrione preparable according to the disclosure of WO 00/21924 is not suitable for the preparation of user-friendly dosage forms. User-friendly dosage forms are, for example, suspension formulations in which tembotrione is present finely milled in solid form. In practical testing it has been found that the tembotrione preparable according to the disclosure of WO 00/21924 leads in suspension formulations to crystal growth and, as a consequence, to clumping and precipitation, so that the suspension formulation becomes unusable. The crystal growth can occur spontaneously or over a longer period and cannot be predicted. The object of the present invention was to provide a modification of tembotrione which overcomes these disadvantages and is suitable for the preparation of a suspension formulation that is storage-stable over a longer period. One subject of the invention is therefore a modification, crystallising in an orthorhombic system, of 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione (tembotrione). In the context of the present invention it was found that, besides the stable modification crystallising in an orthorhombic system, tembotrione also occurs in at least two metastable modifications. Description of the figures. Figure 1 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification I of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 1a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification I of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2. Figure 2 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification II of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 2a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification II of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2. Figure 3 shows the Raman spectrum of crystal modification III of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 1. Figure 3a shows the infrared spectrum of crystal modification III of tembotrione. The values of the band maxima in wavenumbers are listed in Table 2. Table 5: X-ray powder diffractometry pattern of crystal modification I of tembotrione [2θ] Table 6: X-ray powder diffractometry pattern of crystal modification II of tembotrione [2θ] Tembotrione as such can be prepared, for example, by one of the processes named in WO 00/21924. Depending on the nature of the solvent used in the last purification step and on the temperature regime, tembotrione usually crystallises out as a mixture or in the form of a pure one of the metastable crystal modifications II and III described here. Because of its stability, crystal modification I is outstandingly suitable for the preparation of formulations, in particular suspension formulations of crop protection agents. The invention therefore also provides crop protection agents which contain crystal modification I of tembotrione alone or in a mixture with auxiliaries and carriers, and also in a mixture with other active ingredients. The invention also includes mixtures of crystal modification I of tembotrione with crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione, for example those which occur at any point of the conversion process according to the invention of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, into crystal modification I. An active ingredient quality with more than 20 wt.-% of crystal modification I of tembotrione is preferred, particularly preferably with more than 90 wt.-%, very particularly preferably with more than 95 wt.-% and most preferably with more than 98 wt.-%. Because of its stability, crystal modification I of tembotrione is quite generally suitable as starting material for the preparation of any crop protection formulations containing tembotrione, even if after formulation the tembotrione is no longer present in this form but for instance in dissolved form. The invention therefore also provides processes for the preparation of crop protection formulations containing tembotrione which use crystal modification I of tembotrione, and also crop protection formulations containing tembotrione which have been obtained from crystal modification I of tembotrione. The use of crystal modification I increases the safety of preparations of tembotrione and thus reduces the risk of incorrect dosing. Crystal modification I of tembotrione can be converted in a known manner into the customary formulations, such as suspension concentrates, colloidal concentrates, dispersible concentrates, emulsifiable concentrates (emulsion concentrates), emulsion seed dressings, suspension seed dressings, granules, microgranules, suspoemulsions, oil dispersions, water-soluble granules, water-soluble concentrates and water-dispersible granules, using suitable auxiliaries and carriers or solvents. The active compound should here be present in a concentration of about 0.5 to 90 wt.-% of the total mixture, that is to say in amounts which are sufficient to reach the necessary dosage level. The formulations are prepared, for example, by extending crystal modification I of tembotrione with solvents and/or carriers, if appropriate using emulsifiers and/or dispersants, and/or other auxiliaries such as, for example, penetration aids. Tembotrione in crystal modification I exhibits an outstanding herbicidal action against representatives of the group of both monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous plants. The invention therefore also provides the use of crystal modification I of tembotrione for the preparation of a crop protection agent for the treatment of weed infestation. The crystal modification I of tembotrione according to the invention can, as already stated above, be converted into the customary formulations, such as solutions, emulsions, wettable powders, suspensions, powders, dusting agents, pastes, soluble powders, granules, suspension-emulsion concentrates, active-ingredient-impregnated natural and synthetic materials, and also microencapsulations in polymeric materials. The crystal modification I of tembotrione according to the invention can be used as such or in its formulations, also in a mixture with known herbicides and/or with substances which improve crop plant compatibility ("safeners"), for weed control, ready-mix formulations or tank mixes both being possible. Mixtures with weed control agents which contain one or more known herbicides and a safener are therefore also possible. The crystal modification I of tembotrione according to the invention can be applied as such, in the form of its formulations, or in the use forms prepared from these by further dilution, such as ready-to-use solutions, suspensions, emulsions, powders, pastes and granules. A thermodynamically stable crystal modification of the herbicidal active ingredient 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl) cyclohexane-1,3-dione (tembotrione) is described. This thermodynamically stable crystal modification shows particular advantages in the stability of suspension formulations.

More particularly it relates to a thermodynamically stable crystal modification of 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione of the formula [STRUCTURAL FORMULA: see drawings[0]], (hereinafter referred to as tembotrione), processes for its preparation and its use as a herbicide.

The tembotrione known for example from WO 00/21924 (Example No. 3 in Table 1 there) has herbicidal properties and is suitable for the preparation of crop protection agents used for weed control. However, it has been found that the tembotrione preparable according to the disclosure of WO 00/21924 is not suitable for the preparation of user-friendly dosage forms. User-friendly dosage forms are, for example, suspension formulations in which tembotrione is present finely milled in solid form. In practical testing it has been found that the tembotrione preparable according to the disclosure of WO 00/21924 leads in suspension formulations to crystal growth and, as a consequence, to clumping and precipitation, so that the suspension formulation becomes unusable. The crystal growth can occur spontaneously or over a longer period and cannot be predicted.

The object of the present invention was to provide a modification of tembotrione which overcomes these disadvantages and is suitable for the preparation of a suspension formulation that is storage-stable over a longer period.

One subject of the invention is therefore a modification, crystallising in an orthorhombic system, of 2-({2-chloro-4-(methylsulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]phenyl}carbonyl)cyclohexane-1,3-dione (tembotrione).
In the context of the present invention it was found that, besides the stable modification crystallising in an orthorhombic system, tembotrione also occurs in at least two metastable modifications.

Tembotrione as such can be prepared, for example, by one of the processes named in WO 00/21924. Depending on the nature of the solvent used in the last purification step and on the temperature regime, tembotrione usually crystallises out as a mixture or in the form of a pure one of the metastable crystal modifications II and III described here.

Because of its stability, crystal modification I is outstandingly suitable for the preparation of formulations, in particular suspension formulations of crop protection agents. The invention therefore also provides crop protection agents which contain crystal modification I of tembotrione alone or in a mixture with auxiliaries and carriers, and also in a mixture with other active ingredients. The invention also includes mixtures of crystal modification I of tembotrione with crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione, for example those which occur at any point of the conversion process according to the invention of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, into crystal modification I. An active ingredient quality with more than 20 wt.-% of crystal modification I of tembotrione is preferred, particularly preferably with more than 90 wt.-%, very particularly preferably with more than 95 wt.-% and most preferably with more than 98 wt.-%.

Because of its stability, crystal modification I of tembotrione is quite generally suitable as starting material for the preparation of any crop protection formulations containing tembotrione, even if after formulation the tembotrione is no longer present in this form but for instance in dissolved form.

The invention therefore also provides processes for the preparation of crop protection formulations containing tembotrione which use crystal modification I of tembotrione, and also crop protection formulations containing tembotrione which have been obtained from crystal modification I of tembotrione. The use of crystal modification I increases the safety of preparations of tembotrione and thus reduces the risk of incorrect dosing. Crystal modification I of tembotrione can be converted in a known manner into the customary formulations, such as suspension concentrates, colloidal concentrates, dispersible concentrates, emulsifiable concentrates (emulsion concentrates), emulsion seed dressings, suspension seed dressings, granules, microgranules, suspoemulsions, oil dispersions, water-soluble granules, water-soluble concentrates and water-dispersible granules, using suitable auxiliaries and carriers or solvents. The active compound should here be present in a concentration of about 0.5 to 90 wt.-% of the total mixture, that is to say in amounts which are sufficient to reach the necessary dosage level. The formulations are prepared, for example, by extending crystal modification I of tembotrione with solvents and/or carriers, if appropriate using emulsifiers and/or dispersants, and/or other auxiliaries such as, for example, penetration aids.

Tembotrione in crystal modification I exhibits an outstanding herbicidal action against representatives of the group of both monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous plants. The invention therefore also provides the use of crystal modification I of tembotrione for the preparation of a crop protection agent for the treatment of weed infestation.

The crystal modification I of tembotrione according to the invention can, as already stated above, be converted into the customary formulations, such as solutions, emulsions, wettable powders, suspensions, powders, dusting agents, pastes, soluble powders, granules, suspension-emulsion concentrates, active-ingredient-impregnated natural and synthetic materials, and also microencapsulations in polymeric materials.

The crystal modification I of tembotrione according to the invention can be used as such or in its formulations, also in a mixture with known herbicides and/or with substances which improve crop plant compatibility ("safeners"), for weed control, ready-mix formulations or tank mixes both being possible. Mixtures with weed control agents which contain one or more known herbicides and a safener are therefore also possible.

The crystal modification I of tembotrione according to the invention can be applied as such, in the form of its formulations, or in the use forms prepared from these by further dilution, such as ready-to-use solutions, suspensions, emulsions, powders, pastes and granules. Application is carried out in the customary manner, e.g. by pouring, spraying, atomising, scattering.
The crystal modification I of tembotrione according to the invention can be applied both before and after emergence of the plants. It can also be incorporated into the soil before sowing.

claims.evidence_en: Tembotrione as such can be prepared, for example, by one of the processes named in WO 00/21924. Depending on the nature of the solvent used in the last purification step and on the temperature regime, tembotrione usually crystallises out as a mixture or in the form of a pure one of the metastable crystal modifications II and III described here. The thermodynamically stable crystal modification I of tembotrione can in a general manner be so prepared ... in that the crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione obtainable according to WO 00/21924, or mixtures thereof, are suspended and/or dissolved in a suitable solvent and treated at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C until quantitative conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I has occurred. A further subject of the invention is thus a process for the preparation of the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I of tembotrione, in which the crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione, or mixtures thereof, are suspended and/or dissolved in solvents and treated at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C until quantitative conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I has occurred. Suitable solvents which can be used in this process are, for example, lower alcohols such as methanol, ethanol, 2-propanol, or ketones such as acetone, 2-butanone, which can also be used in a mixture with water. Lower alcohols and ketones here denote those compounds which have one to ten carbon atoms, preferably one to five carbon atoms. Further suitable solvents are benzene, toluene and chlorobenzene. The conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I takes place at temperatures below 100°C, preferably at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C, particularly preferably at temperatures of 60°C to 80°C, very particularly preferably at temperatures of 50°C to 80°C. The duration of the conversion depends on the temperature and on the type of solvent. The duration of the conversion further depends on whether seed crystals of crystal modification I are used. In general, when the crystals of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, are completely dissolved at elevated temperature, the conversion into crystal modification I can be achieved directly by cooling crystallisation to room temperature without the use of seed crystals. Cooling to room temperature is preferably carried out at a cooling rate of less than 25°C, particularly preferably at a cooling rate of less than 20°C. The conversion of a suspension of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, can as a rule be brought about within a period of 14 days without the use of seed crystals. If seed crystals of crystal modification I are used in the conversion of a suspension, a treatment time of 24 to 48 hours is in general sufficient to achieve quantitative conversion of the crystals into crystal modification I. The crystals of crystal modification I obtained are finally separated off and dried at room temperature or elevated temperature to constant weight in order to remove the solvent.

claims.evidence_en: Because of its stability, crystal modification I is outstandingly suitable for the preparation of formulations, in particular suspension formulations of crop protection agents. The invention therefore also provides crop protection agents which contain crystal modification I of tembotrione alone or in a mixture with auxiliaries and carriers, and also in a mixture with other active ingredients. The invention also includes mixtures of crystal modification I of tembotrione with crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione, for example those which occur at any point of the conversion process according to the invention of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, into crystal modification I. An active ingredient quality with more than 20 wt.-% of crystal modification I of tembotrione is preferred, particularly preferably with more than 90 wt.-%, very particularly preferably with more than 95 wt.-% and most preferably with more than 98 wt.-%. Because of its stability, crystal modification I of tembotrione is quite generally suitable as starting material for the preparation of any crop protection formulations containing tembotrione, even if after formulation the tembotrione is no longer present in this form but for instance in dissolved form. The invention therefore also provides processes for the preparation of crop protection formulations containing tembotrione which use crystal modification I of tembotrione, and also crop protection formulations containing tembotrione which have been obtained from crystal modification I of tembotrione. The use of crystal modification I increases the safety of preparations of tembotrione and thus reduces the risk of incorrect dosing. Crystal modification I of tembotrione can be converted in a known manner into the customary formulations, such as suspension concentrates, colloidal concentrates, dispersible concentrates, emulsifiable concentrates (emulsion concentrates), emulsion seed dressings, suspension seed dressings, granules, microgranules, suspoemulsions, oil dispersions, water-soluble granules, water-soluble concentrates and water-dispersible granules, using suitable auxiliaries and carriers or solvents. The active compound should here be present in a concentration of about 0.5 to 90 wt.-% of the total mixture, that is to say in amounts which are sufficient to reach the necessary dosage level. The formulations are prepared, for example, by extending crystal modification I of tembotrione with solvents and/or carriers, if appropriate using emulsifiers and/or dispersants, and/or other auxiliaries such as, for example, penetration aids.

claims.evidence_en: The tembotrione known for example from WO 00/21924 (Example No. 3 in Table 1 there) has herbicidal properties and is suitable for the preparation of crop protection agents used for weed control. However, it has been found that the tembotrione preparable according to the disclosure of WO 00/21924 is not suitable for the preparation of user-friendly dosage forms. User-friendly dosage forms are, for example, suspension formulations in which tembotrione is present finely milled in solid form. In practical testing it has been found that the tembotrione preparable according to the disclosure of WO 00/21924 leads in suspension formulations to crystal growth and, as a consequence, to clumping and precipitation, so that the suspension formulation becomes unusable. The crystal growth can occur spontaneously or over a longer period and cannot be predicted. The object of the present invention was to provide a modification of tembotrione which overcomes these disadvantages and is suitable for the preparation of a suspension formulation that is storage-stable over a longer period.

claims.evidence_en: Tembotrione as such can be prepared, for example, by one of the processes named in WO 00/21924. Depending on the nature of the solvent used in the last purification step and on the temperature regime, tembotrione usually crystallises out as a mixture or in the form of a pure one of the metastable crystal modifications II and III described here. The thermodynamically stable crystal modification I of tembotrione can in a general manner be so prepared ... in that the crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione obtainable according to WO 00/21924, or mixtures thereof, are suspended and/or dissolved in a suitable solvent and treated at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C until quantitative conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I has occurred. A further subject of the invention is thus a process for the preparation of the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I of tembotrione, in which the crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione, or mixtures thereof, are suspended and/or dissolved in solvents and treated at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C until quantitative conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I has occurred. Suitable solvents which can be used in this process are, for example, lower alcohols such as methanol, ethanol, 2-propanol, or ketones such as acetone, 2-butanone, which can also be used in a mixture with water. Lower alcohols and ketones here denote those compounds which have one to ten carbon atoms, preferably one to five carbon atoms. Further suitable solvents are benzene, toluene and chlorobenzene. The conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I takes place at temperatures below 100°C, preferably at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C, particularly preferably at temperatures of 60°C to 80°C, very particularly preferably at temperatures of 50°C to 80°C. The duration of the conversion depends on the temperature and on the type of solvent. The duration of the conversion further depends on whether seed crystals of crystal modification I are used. In general, when the crystals of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, are completely dissolved at elevated temperature, the conversion into crystal modification I can be achieved directly by cooling crystallisation to room temperature without the use of seed crystals. Cooling to room temperature is preferably carried out at a cooling rate of less than 25°C, particularly preferably at a cooling rate of less than 20°C. The conversion of a suspension of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, can as a rule be brought about within a period of 14 days without the use of seed crystals. If seed crystals of crystal modification I are used in the conversion of a suspension, a treatment time of 24 to 48 hours is in general sufficient to achieve quantitative conversion of the crystals into crystal modification I. The crystals of crystal modification I obtained are finally separated off and dried at room temperature or elevated temperature to constant weight in order to remove the solvent.

claims.evidence_en: The preferred transgenic (genetically modified) plants or plant cultivars to be treated according to the invention include all plants which, through the genetic modification, received genetic material that confers particularly advantageous, useful properties ("traits") on these plants. Examples of such properties are better plant growth, increased tolerance to high or low temperatures, increased tolerance to drought or to water or soil salt content, increased flowering performance, easier harvesting, acceleration of ripening, higher crop yields, higher quality and/or higher nutritional value of the harvested products, better storability and/or processability of the harvested products. Further and particularly emphasised examples of such properties are an increased defence of the plants against animal and microbial pests, such as against insects, mites, phytopathogenic fungi, bacteria and/or viruses, and also an increased tolerance of the plants to certain herbicidal active ingredients. Examples of transgenic plants mentioned are the important crop plants, such as cereals (wheat, rice), soya, potato, cotton, oilseed rape and in particular maize, and also fruit plants (with the fruits apples, pears, citrus fruits and grapes), maize in particular, but also soya, potato, cotton and oilseed rape, being especially emphasised. Properties ("traits") especially emphasised are the increased defence of the plants against insects by toxins formed in the plants, in particular those which are produced in the plants by the genetic material from Bacillus thuringiensis (for example by the genes CrylA(a), CrylA(b), CrylA(c), CryIIA, CrylIIIA, CrylIIIB2, Cry9c, Cry2Ab, Cry3Bb and CrylF, and combinations thereof) (hereinafter "Bt plants"). Properties ("traits") also especially emphasised are the increased defence of plants against fungi, bacteria and viruses by systemic acquired resistance (SAR), systemin, phytoalexins, elicitors, and also resistance genes and correspondingly expressed proteins and toxins. Properties ("traits") furthermore especially emphasised are the increased tolerance of the plants to certain herbicidal active ingredients, for example imidazolinones, sulfonylureas, glyphosate or phosphinothricin (for example the "PAT" gene). The genes conferring the respective desired properties ("traits") may also occur in combination with one another in the transgenic plants. Examples of "Bt plants" which may be mentioned are above all maize varieties, but likewise cotton varieties, soya varieties and potato varieties, sold under the trade names YIELD GARD(R) (for example maize, cotton, soya), KnockOut(R) (for example maize), StarLink(R) (for example maize), Bollgard(R) (cotton), Nucotn(R) (cotton) and NewLeaf(R) (potato). Examples of herbicide-tolerant plants which may be mentioned are above all maize varieties, but likewise cotton varieties and soya varieties, sold under the trade names Roundup Ready(R) (tolerance to glyphosate, for example maize, cotton, soya), Liberty Link(R) (tolerance to phosphinothricin, for example oilseed rape), IMI(R) (tolerance to imidazolinones) and STS(R) (tolerance to sulfonylureas, for example maize). Herbicide-resistant plants (bred conventionally for herbicide tolerance) which may be mentioned also include the varieties sold under the name Clearfield(R) (for example maize). It goes without saying that these statements also apply to plant cultivars developed in the future, or coming onto the market in the future, having these or genetic properties developed in the future ("traits").

This thermodynamically stable crystal modification shows particular advantages in the stability of suspension formulations.

The tembotrione known for example from WO 00/21924 (Example No. 3 in Table 1 there) has herbicidal properties and is suitable for the preparation of crop protection agents used for weed control. However, it has been found that the tembotrione preparable according to the disclosure of WO 00/21924 is not suitable for the preparation of user-friendly dosage forms. User-friendly dosage forms are, for example, suspension formulations in which tembotrione is present finely milled in solid form. In practical testing it has been found that the tembotrione preparable according to the disclosure of WO 00/21924 leads in suspension formulations to crystal growth and, as a consequence, to clumping and precipitation, so that the suspension formulation becomes unusable. The crystal growth can occur spontaneously or over a longer period and cannot be predicted.

A further subject of the invention is thus a process for the preparation of the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I of tembotrione, in which the crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione, or mixtures thereof, are suspended and/or dissolved in solvents and treated at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C until quantitative conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I has occurred.

A further subject of the invention is thus a process for the preparation of the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I of tembotrione, in which the crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione, or mixtures thereof, are suspended and/or dissolved in solvents and treated at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C until quantitative conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I has occurred.

Suitable solvents which can be used in this process are, for example, lower alcohols such as methanol, ethanol, 2-propanol, or ketones such as acetone, 2-butanone, which can also be used in a mixture with water. Lower alcohols and ketones here denote those compounds which have one to ten carbon atoms, preferably one to five carbon atoms. Further suitable solvents are benzene, toluene and chlorobenzene.

The conversion into the thermodynamically stable crystal modification I takes place at temperatures below 100°C, preferably at temperatures of 0°C to 80°C, particularly preferably at temperatures of 60°C to 80°C, very particularly preferably at temperatures of 50°C to 80°C. The duration of the conversion depends on the temperature and on the type of solvent. The duration of the conversion further depends on whether seed crystals of crystal modification I are used. In general, when the crystals of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, are completely dissolved at elevated temperature, the conversion into crystal modification I can be achieved directly by cooling crystallisation to room temperature without the use of seed crystals. Cooling to room temperature is preferably carried out at a cooling rate of less than 25°C, particularly preferably at a cooling rate of less than 20°C. The conversion of a suspension of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, can as a rule be brought about within a period of 14 days without the use of seed crystals. If seed crystals of crystal modification I are used in the conversion of a suspension, a treatment time of 24 to 48 hours is in general sufficient to achieve quantitative conversion of the crystals into crystal modification I.

Because of its stability, crystal modification I is outstandingly suitable for the preparation of formulations, in particular suspension formulations of crop protection agents. The invention therefore also provides crop protection agents which contain crystal modification I of tembotrione alone or in a mixture with auxiliaries and carriers, and also in a mixture with other active ingredients. The invention also includes mixtures of crystal modification I of tembotrione with crystal modifications II and III of tembotrione, for example those which occur at any point of the conversion process according to the invention of crystal modifications II and III, or mixtures thereof, into crystal modification I. An active ingredient quality with more than 20 wt.-% of crystal modification I of tembotrione is preferred, particularly preferably with more than 90 wt.-%, very particularly preferably with more than 95 wt.-% and most preferably with more than 98 wt.-%.

lines.section_en: Mixtures with Known Herbicides and Safeners
